text:
maria: Heads-up: nightly perf regression on TP mixed-precision suite after the kernel-path selector change. p99 latency up ~12% and all-reduce time roughly doubled. Anyone else seeing this?

devon: which selector change? the prefer_mlir flip I merged last night?

maria: Yeah — I flipped `prefer_mlir=true` in kernel_selector for TP kernels. Nightly 8xA100 runs show a clear spike.

akshay: Can you paste the numbers (p50/p95/p99) + allreduce breakdown?

maria: Here are the profiler snippets from the failing job:
```
run: nightly/tp-mp-int8-8gpu
p50: 23.1ms -> 24.0ms (+3.9%)
p95: 44.5ms -> 50.2ms (+12.9%)
p99: 78.9ms -> 88.5ms (+12.2%)
allreduce avg: 4.2ms -> 9.8ms
nvlink bw per step: 62GB/s -> 28GB/s
kv_cache_hit: 87% -> 61%
batcher: auto (seq dist skewed)
```

devon: :eyes: that NVLink drop is massive. Could the MLIR path be emitting a different partitioning that creates lots of small allreduces?

sasha: MLIR path added a fused matmul+softmax kernel — compute edges look better but the output sharding changed. We're seeing more small-shard allreduces instead of fewer large ones.

akshay: That would explain throughput collapse. Also noticed the batcher heuristic change last week groups by `approx_token_bucket` and can split prefixes — this can lead to KV cache invalidations and extra comm.

maria: KV trace excerpt:
```
[KV] miss seq=128 step=342 uid=0x7f2a -> invalidate prefix cache (reason=batch-split)
[KV] miss seq=64 step=343 uid=0x7f2a -> new cache entry created
torch.distributed.all_reduce: 10.12ms (calls 4620)
torch.distributed.broadcast: 1.1ms
```

perf-bot: profiling artifact uploaded: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/2065432100 (flamegraph + nvprof)

devon: flamegraph shows a hot vertical from `ncclAllReduce` at many small sizes (~1-8KB). NCCL performance is terrible for lots of tiny reductions — P2P overhead dominates.

sasha: Quick local check: toggling `prefer_mlir=false` on the same model reduces allreduce to ~4.3ms and restores nvlink bw. So MLIR path looks like the trigger.

akshay: Proposed fixes: 
  1) revert MLIR flip in kernel_selector until we fix shard packing.
  2) in batcher, add a `prefix-preserve` mode so we don't split sequences that keep KV cache warm.
  3) implement `comm_coalesce` window: coalesce small allreduces into a buffered larger allreduce when safe.

maria: I'm rolling back the prefer_mlir flip in main now and kicking off a canary. Opening a follow-up PR to add `comm_coalesce` and `kv_preserve` flags for the batcher.

devon: Add a perf regression ticket and block the MLIR flip on CI until we have microbenchmarks proving no NVLink regression. :thumbsup:

sasha: I'll run microbenchmarks focusing on FP8 packing/alignment costs and the change in shard boundary offsets; might be an alignment/padding bug causing extra transfers.

maria: Thanks all — will post canary numbers here. If the rollback looks good, we'll gate MLIR path behind sequence-length/routing heuristics rather than a global flip.
